data.narrative:
Viam, a Series C robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Eliot Horowitz, has raised $117M to date. The valuation analysis draws on two methods triangulated against a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, all operating in adjacent stages (Series B through Series D).

The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $117M capital base, yielding $199M. The peer-median approach examines 7 same-sector peers at comparable stages—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dextejust ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—establishing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The discrepancy between methods reflects stage positioning ambiguity relative to the peer set, which spans Series B through Series D.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $169M (floor, conservative stage-progression) to $1.9B (ceiling, peer median at high range), with a median estimate of $924M. The wide band reflects uncertainty around whether Viam should be valued toward earlier-stage fundamentals or peer multiples. Key variables include revenue scale relative to peer benchmarks, customer concentration, and capital efficiency metrics—none provided in available data.
